extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, poets, and readers interested in principles of poetic composition and periodical criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and judging poetry and for conducting periodical literary criticism: announcing principles, supporting judgments, and stylistic norms for poetic composition and review. Emphasizes ethical, argumentative, and aesthetic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation fair and philosophical
rubrics_metrics.description: A fair and philosophical investigation is one in which the critic announces and endeavours to establish the principles he holds for the foundation of poetry in general, with specification of these in their application to the different classes of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare canons of criticism for praise and condemnation; particularize striking passages to which the canons apply; faithfully note frequent or infrequent recurrence of merits or defects; distinguish characteristic features from accidental ones; ensure premises are rational, deductions legitimate, and conclusions justly applied; if errors exist, present them definitely and tangibly so others can detect them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce principles before judging
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic should state his principles and how they apply before passing judgment on works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make one's critical theory explicit so readers can see the grounds of praise or blame rather than encountering unsupported sweeping assertions. Example: the critic should have established leading principles rather than proceeding from prophecy like 'This won't do!'

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularize with illustrative extracts and show derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: When extracting passages to illustrate faults or merits, the critic must show from which general grounds or rules the faultiness or excellence is deduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extracts that are divorced from any general rule; supply quotations that prove the point and explain how the passage exemplifies the alleged quality. Mere assertion without quotation or explanatory deduction is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assertion in place of argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism must rely on argument and proof rather than bare assertions or petulant verdicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute arbitrary condemnation for reasoned demonstration; provide supporting quotations and logical deductions. The reviewer should not deliver an unargued sentence of condemnation or call lines 'raving' without showing why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not read preconceptions into extracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics must not select or prick passages to fit preconceived opinions; the critique should follow reading, not precede it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the impression that the review was written before the work was read and that extracts were chosen after the fact to illustrate preconceived points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep criticism impersonal and limited to publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique should address the publication as the impersonation of the work under trial and avoid personal allusions or use of private knowledge about the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude personal attacks and recollections of the author's life beyond what appears in publications; using more intimate knowledge makes censure a personal injury and degrades the critic into a gossip or pasquinade. No recommitment of juvenile performances from long past ought to be used to assail an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic must weigh words to achieve intended effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic is authorized to be harsh or mild according to the effect he intends to produce but must choose his phrases deliberately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer is authorized to reply but not to complain about phrase softness or hardness; the critic must understand the effect he seeks and measure his language accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to announced plan and scope of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodical reviews should be faithful to their announced plan—reviewing only works susceptible and deserving of argumentative criticism and supplying original essays where suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reviewing trifling works without merit simply to vent dislike or increase sales; do not misuse the review's authority to rehash negligible works or to flatter malign passions for circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground criticism on universal morals and philosophic reason (institutional code)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collective reviewing body should administer judgment according to a constitution and code grounded on universal morals and philosophical reason, speaking as representatives of their body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics in a learned committee should lay aside individuality and judge by shared, rational standards rather than partisan or personal bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unjustified revival of past juvenile works
rubrics_metrics.description: Forcing back juvenile performances into public notice without clear motive is improper and suggests personal malignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not re-commit or re-publish forgotten youthful works for vindictive reasons; such conduct is likely driven by personal spite or wanton malignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge truths in an opponent's theory and measure their influence
rubrics_metrics.description: When refuting a poet's theory, give due credit to the truths in it and examine how extensively the mistaken theory has influenced the poet's compositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show whether errors are diffuse or isolated, whether infected passages are numerous or trifling, and whether the faults are woven into works or separable; this measured approach prevents exaggerated charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's office: select the most dignified and weighty subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet should choose subjects of dignity and weight—poetry's proper object is the intense, weighty, and philosophical product of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry aims at the most intense and abstract presentation of human experience; the poet should avoid dwelling chiefly on the low, mean, or trivial as a sustained habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency of style; avoid sudden inconstancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid sudden and unprepared transitions from striking poetic lines to an undistinguished, neutral, or prose-like style; maintain a consistent poetic diction appropriate to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language may be divided into poetic, prosaic, and neutral; abrupt alternation between them startles the reader and produces anticlimax and hyperclimax. Keep high poetic passages suitably framed (e.g., Metastasio placed arias at ends of scenes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not intermingle prose and verse without design
rubrics_metrics.description: Passing from verse to prose or to neutral language within the same composition without clear artistic justification is awkward and displeasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such alternations should be deliberate and justified by form (e.g., inserted songs) rather than sudden shifts that interrupt the reader's prepared expectation of the mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid matter-of-fact minuteness and over-description
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist laborious minuteness and fidelity in the representation of objects and positions that burden poetic imagination; the poet should paint to the imagination, not to the fancy-like detail of an artisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive local imagery and precise, diagram-like description cause reader fatigue; prefer creative, whole-picture presentation (Milton's creations) over dissected, map-like detail. Use description only when necessary for intelligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive biographical particularity for poetic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not introduce elaborate birth, parentage, and minute biography to justify a character in poetry; poets' characters should remain representative rather than excessively individualized by biography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-specific life-histories (as in certain novels) break the poetic illusion and force the reader into disbelief; such biographical exposition suits biography or novels of certain kinds, not representative poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve poetic 'illusion' and negative faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the reader's poetic belief (negative faith) by avoiding proximity of exotic verifiable facts or historical particulars that would extinguish poetic illusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate neighbouring of words and facts of absolute truth can repel the reader's willing belief; the poet should avoid mixing verifiable historical truth too closely with fictional/poetic elements that depend on imaginative assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use character choice to serve poetic ends, not moralizing sermonizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing humble or low-life characters to prove a moral thesis is suspect when the immediate object is moral philosophy rather than poetic pleasure; poetry's primary means is to give pleasure through general associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the poet's aim is primarily moral persuasion (as in sermons or essays), the choice of character may be better suited to prose genres; poetry should not be reduced to didactic moral instruction at the cost of aesthetic effect.
